prompt: A sample's IR shows a sharp, narrow O–H band at ~3620 cm⁻¹ (not the usual broad peak at 3200-3550). The sample is MOST likely:

options.label: A dilute solution of an alcohol in a nonpolar solvent (isolated non-H-bonded O-H)
A pure carboxylic acid showing the sharp monomer form rather than the dimer
Water, whose O-H appears sharper at this wavenumber due to its small size
A phenol — the aromatic ring's rigidity sharpens the O-H band

explanation: H-bonded O-H is broad (because the H-bond varies in strength → range of O-H frequencies). Non-H-bonded O-H is sharp and higher (~3620). You get this by diluting the alcohol in CCl₄ or CS₂ (nonpolar, no acceptor). Pure COOH, water, and phenol all H-bond strongly and give broad peaks.
